log.msg: Both buttons proved headless on this task's own page at 1280: Approve on smoke-test wrote {"verdict": {say:"approve"}} into this very task.jsonl through rpc:append, the line came back off the socket, TaskJSONL.judged() merged it onto the decision, and the row went open -> APPROVED with no reload; Improve on rule-chip took a one-line note the same way. Head counts moved 7 waiting -> 1 approved / 1 to improve / 5 waiting. Two numbers agree: 7 decision lines in the log, 7 rows on the tab.

Two real defects found by measuring rather than reading. (1) --wash IS the app ground in this theme (styles.css: .app { background: var(--wash) }, lew42 --wash #f2f2f2), so the first ui/decision painted three option boxes that measured rgb(242,242,242) against a rgb(242,242,242) page - invisible, and the owner's whole box rule silently unmet. Options are --surface + a 2px border now, the chosen one a warm color-mix ground plus an accent border plus the word chosen (three cues, because --prim is 2.96:1 on white and may carry neither text nor a UI shape). (2) say is the button's word (approve) and status is the decision's state (approved): the head counted 0 approved until judged() reconciled them.

assign.outcome:
**Every decision is now a claim tree the owner can Approve or Improve, and an Improve goes back to the rule that caused it.**

A worker writes down a choice and the alternatives it was made over; the task page grows a **Decisions** tab; the owner presses a button; a CLI carries an Improve into that skill's `improvements.md`. Six pieces, all live.

- **The `decision` and `verdict` verbs** — [`ext/JSONL`](/framework/ext/JSONL/), merged by `id` like `ask`. A decision is the question, the options, the one chosen, why, and the rule. A verdict is the owner's press, its own line, never an edit. [The shape](/framework/ext/JSONL/doc/task-jsonl/).
- **The Decisions tab** — after Asks, before Report, only when a task carries decisions. [This task's own](/framework/ai/2026-09-17/decisions-system/) · [the run's](/framework/ai/2026-09-17/mastermind-layout-browser/). A press appends a `verdict` to that task's own log through `rpc:append`; the row updates over the socket with no reload; the buttons are not drawn off the dev server.
- **[`ui/decision`](/framework/ui/decision/)** — the template: the options as cards with a ground each, the chosen one marked three ways (warm ground, accent border, the word *chosen*) because the accent is 2.96:1 on white and may carry neither text nor a shape.
- **`decisions.mjs`** — `node public/framework/ext/AITask/decisions.mjs file` turns every unfiled Improve whose decision names a rule into one dated line in that skill's `improvements.md`, then marks it filed. The mastermind runs it at harvest. [Why a CLI](/framework/ext/AITask/doc/decisions-tab/).
- **The skills produce it** — one line each in `code` and `layout`: every choice between alternatives is a `decision` line.
- **The first tree** — this run's six decisions in [`run-decisions.jsonl`](/framework/ai/2026-09-17/decisions-system/run-decisions.jsonl), for the mastermind to append to its own log.
- **Plus, mid-task:** the Asks wall is now grouped by an ask's `topic` — five bands, 34 cards for 34 asks.

**Two defects found by measuring.** `--wash` *is* the app ground (`.app { background: var(--wash) }`), so the first option cards painted rgb(242,242,242) on a rgb(242,242,242) page — invisible. And `say` (the button) is not `status` (the decision's state), so the tab counted zero approvals until `judged()` reconciled them.

**Left for the owner.** The rule is a **chip, not a link** — skills live outside `public/` and nothing serves them; a dev-only route that would make it a real link is logged here as an open decision. The two verdicts already in this log were pressed by the build as its smoke test, not by the owner; the Improve says so in its own note, and the newest press always wins.
